title: Heterogeneous-Quant Smoke & Sensitivity Suite for INT8 Weight-Only (GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Samantha Lee
description: Goal: Build a compact, reproducible smoke and sensitivity validation suite that verifies INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quantization profiles across a heterogeneous set of target runtimes and hardware, catches accuracy regressions early, and produces per-layer sensitivity heatmaps and statistical pass/fail signals for CI and canary rollouts. This ticket focuses on integration-level tests and regression automation (not the research experiments for novel quant formats). We want tests that are fast enough for presubmit and nightly gates but thorough enough to flag distributional failures and performance-sensitive layers.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible smoke harness runs in <= 20 minutes for a single model+profile on A100/H100 and a CPU fallback, producing token-level perplexity and top-k match metrics.
Per-layer sensitivity heatmaps (CSV + compact PNG) generated for each run and uploaded to the regression dashboard for visual comparison.
Automated statistical test: paired-sample test between baseline FP16 run and INT8 quantized run with configurable alpha; default alpha=0.01 and minimum sample size calculation included.
CI gating: a nightly job that runs a representative model matrix (small/medium/large) and opens a regression issue if metric drift exceeds configurable thresholds.
Compatibility matrix: same test produces a pass/fail report for kernel/runtime combinations (cuda-11.8+nvcuda, cuda-12+h100 kernels, cpu-avx2) and lists recommended fallback variants.
Documentation: a concise runbook and 'how to add a model' guide committed to the quant-profiles docs page with example commands and expected artifact locations.
test_plan: Create a minimal harness wrapper that runs: (1) fp16 baseline, (2) GPTQ INT8 W-only, (3) AWQ INT8 W-only where available; outputs token-level logprobs and decoded generations.
Generate 3 deterministic prompt sets: general chat, code completion, and arithmetic reasoning (100 seeds each). Prompts stored in /confluence/quant-profiles/prompt-sets.
Collect metrics: perplexity, mean token logprob delta, top-1/top-5 token-match, and BLEU for code tasks. Save raw outputs to GCS for later diffing.
Compute per-layer delta distributions by comparing intermediate activations (where available) and aggregate into a heatmap and sensitivity score.
Run across hardware matrix: A100 (cuda-11.8), H100 (cuda-12), and CPU reference. Use simulated low-memory & high-latency knobs for stress tests.
Automate paired statistical tests (Wilcoxon or paired t-test depending on distribution) and embed p-values and effect sizes in the artifacts JSON.
Fail criteria: mean token logprob delta > 0.12 or p-value < 0.01 for primary prompt set OR any regression in top-1 match > 3% on code tasks.
Wrap harness as a reproducible Docker image and publish to our internal registry with tags: quant-smoke:v{semver}, e.g., quant-smoke:v1.0.0.
Expose an opt-in flag to run longer 'safety' comparisons for nightly jobs that increase sample counts by 5x.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Presubmit): provide a lightweight binary smoke that runs on changed-model PRs (subset of prompts, single hardware). If presubmit fails, it blocks merge.
Phase 2 (Nightly): run full matrix nightly with extended samples; failures create an automated regression issue and tag the model/profile owner.

Phase 3 (Canary): when a new quant profile is promoted, run 24h canary on a fraction of traffic using runtime-1.22 with telemetry hooks to capture token-level errors; fallback policy in place to revert to FP16 variant on severe regressions.
Rollback: documented playbook with steps to mark profile as deprecated, remove from routing table, and open a postmortem if customer impact observed.
